items.raw_snippet: * Startup E42 creates marketplace for companies to hire artificial intelligence workers. # Startup E42 creates marketplace for companies to hire AI workers. Studies show by 2026 at least 50 per cent of the enterprise workforce will be AI workers. Enterprises and companies across sectors will soon be able to recruit artificial intelligence (AI) workers from the internet, just like hiring personnel from employment portals. AI focussed startup E42 has announced it is setting up a marketplace for AI workers where companies can explore and hire AI bots offering basic services such as receptionist, customer care executives, selling agents to more complex ones such HR executives, IT operations manager, lab assistants, analysts among others. Animesh Samuel, co-founder and CEO, E42, said at the launch of the platform, various studies show by 2026 at least 50 per cent of the enterprise workforce will be AI workers, opening up a $800 billion industry business opportunity. The aim of the E42 marketplace would be to create a platform like Naukri or Monster but for hiring AI workers. “Already around 40 odd AI workers are there as of pre-launch. By the third quarter, we should be having around 150 AI workers available for deployment,” said Samuel. E42 co-founder and CTO Sanjeev Menon said that AI workers today are able to connect various data sources and generate insights on various interactions. Menon said that being a no-code natural language processing (NLP) platform, there is flexibility for E42 platform to customise the AI workers as per the requirement of the enterprise. They are able to add their subject matter expertise into the platform and create AI workers to automate specific workers within the organisation,” Menon said. E42 has already seen more than 50 per cent of the customer interaction happening for some of the companies through AI and Menon said that this is expected to increase as AI adoption makes a transition from an aspirational aspect to an essential utility for companies. * ## Northeast students seek shield from slurs, hold protest over death of Tripura youth. * ## Kolkata’s contradictions: Why young residents stay, love it, and seek change.

# Krutrim to Release AI Chips by 2026. Krutrim to Release AI Chips by 2026. On Thursday, Ola co-founder and CEO Bhavish Aggarwal stated that India must establish its future on its own terms in order to dominate the technologies of the future, specifically mentioning artificial intelligence (AI). At a press conference in Hosur, where new products were unveiled by Ola's electric vehicle, cab, and artificial intelligence divisions, he predicted that the company would "simply end up becoming monthly active user farms for global companies" if current trends carry on. Krutrim, an artificial intelligence division of the Bengaluru-based business, plans to produce India's first AI silicon chip by the year 2026. In order to construct the chips, Ola established strategic alliances with multinational powerhouses including ARM, a chip design firm, and Untether AI, an artificial intelligence firm based in Canada. A video message was played at the Hosur ceremony by ARM CEO Rene Haas, who expressed his joy at the partnership with Ola Krutrim. The Bodhi AI chip, the Sarv general-purpose CPU, and the Ojas edge-computing CPU are all part of Krutrim's first family of semiconductors. As an additional resource for the developer community, Krutrim has introduced Krutrim Cloud, which offers general-purpose and AI capabilities along with a variety of AI services designed specifically for product development. Ola Consumer is the new name for Aggarwal's initial ride-sharing company, Ola Cabs. For all ONDC vendors, including startups and SMEs, Ola Consumer is offering a free year of Krutrim Cloud. In a test program that ended this year, Ola Food & Grocery on ONDC exceeded 40,000 orders daily in Bengaluru. items.raw_snippet: It has been translated through NAVER # detail It has been translated through NAVER : 2024-06-03 16:38:32 : 2024-06-03 19:58:46 Jensen Huang CEO 'Computex' Presents Nvidia unveils next-generation AI chip 'Rubin' New product launch 2 years → 1 year Competition between Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix is likely to intensify. Nvidia, a leading artificial intelligence (AI) chip company, unveiled its next-generation AI graphics processing device (GPU) Rubin for the first time. Even before the AI chip platform "Blackwell" was mass-produced, it announced plans to launch the next-generation platform, strengthening its market dominance. The Rubin, which will be released in 2026, is expected to be equipped with HBM4, the next-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM). NVIDIA Founder and CEO Jensen Huang introduced "Rubin" in his keynote speech at Nvidia Computex 2024 at the National Taipei University Gymnasium in Taipei, Taiwan, on the 2nd (local time). CEO Hwang said, "NVIDIA is leading the wave of next-generation technology development beyond the limits of its potential with innovations in AI and accelerated computing." Earlier, Nvidia released AI chip B100 based on high-performance GPU 'Blackwell'. Previously, Nvidia has introduced new products every two years, but CEO Hwang announced on the same day that he would shorten the launch of the product by half to one year. CEO Hwang said, "NVIDIA's rhythm is every year," adding, "The basic philosophy is to build the entire data center size, sell components every year, and push everything to the limit of technology." Nvidia will soon officially operate the Blackwell GPU's platform, followed by the release of the Blackwell Ultra version in 2025. In particular, CEO Hwang said that he will mass-produce "Rubin," the next-generation GPU, from 2026. Both companies are expected to focus on developing HBM4 technology and completing mass production in time for Rubin's launch. Just as much as Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, competition between Nvidia and AMD over the AI chip market is also drawing attention. AMD CEO Lisa Su expressed confidence on the 3rd as a keynote speaker at Computex 2024, saying that the next-generation AI chip "MI350," which will be released next year, will perform 1.2 times better than Nvidia's Blackwell B200.
